title: I Took the Community-Theater Prop Checkout to the Lead Who Hoarded Swords

parts.text: I opened the prop cage at 5:48 p.m. and three foils were tagged OUT under Miles, the lead, with no return stamp. The clipboard said: ONE WEAPON PER ROLE. RETURN AFTER NOTES. I was thirty-four, props volunteer, holding Act Two without a blade. Miles palmed a fourth into his tote. "Leads are the fight." I photographed the tags, the clipboard, and the tote. Then I logged a checkout exception. At 6:01 the stage manager asked why Miles's name was on four foils. I asked once, then I documented twice. The second photo is for the person who will say they never saw the first.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The stage manager can see four foils tagged to Miles against the one-weapon clipboard.

social.video_title: He checked out four foils on a one-weapon clipboard — Part 1/2
social.description: Community theater, a lead's tote, and a clipboard he signed. I logged the exception. Would you have opened the cage?

parts.text: Miles called it rehearsal until fight call asked for the log. I printed the tags, the photo, and the clipboard. Three foils came back. Miles fought with one like the understudy and told notes that leads were always about optics. Optics is a word leads use when a tote exists. Checkout now has a second line: LEADS ARE NOT THE ARMORY. I keep a labeled rack. Miles signs one line. The cage finally looks like props, not a closet. The room sounds like a room again, not a title. Petty is a word people use when their name is on the ticket.

social.video_title: Leads are not the armory — Part 2/2
social.description: Fight call, returned foils, and a second line. Was rehearsal ever four swords?
